metadata.title: Convergence of a splitting inertial proximal method for monotone operators

items.name: Sum of two operators
items.statement:
For two set-valued operators \(A, B : H \rightrightarrows H\), their sum \(A + B\) is defined by
\[(A + B)(x) := \{a + b : a \in A(x),\; b \in B(x)\}.\]

items.name: Monotone operator
items.statement: An operator \(T\) on a real Hilbert space \(H\) is said to be monotone if \(\langle u - v, x - y \rangle \ge 0\) whenever \(u \in T(x), v \in T(y)\).

items.name: Graph of a set-valued operator
items.statement:
The graph of a set-valued operator \(T : H \rightrightarrows H\) on a Hilbert space \(H\) is the set
\[\operatorname{gra} T := \{(x, y) \in H \times H : y \in T(x)\}.\]

items.name: Inverse of a set-valued operator
items.statement:
For a set-valued operator \(T : H \rightrightarrows H\), its inverse \(T^{-1}\) is defined by
\[T^{-1}(y) := \{x \in H : y \in T(x)\}.\]

items.name: ε-enlargement of a monotone operator
items.statement:
For a monotone operator \(T\) and \(\varepsilon \ge 0\), the \(\varepsilon\)-enlargement \(T_{\varepsilon}\) is defined by
\[T_{\varepsilon}(x) := \{v \in H : \langle u - v, y - x \rangle \ge -\varepsilon \;\forall y, \forall u \in T(y)\}. \tag{1.5}\]
Since \(T\) is assumed to be maximal monotone, \(T_0(x) = T(x)\) for any \(x\). Furthermore, directly from the definition it follows that
\[0 \le \varepsilon_1 \le \varepsilon_2 \Rightarrow T_{\varepsilon_1}(x) \subset T_{\varepsilon_2}(x).\]

items.name: Maximal monotone operator
items.statement: An operator \(T\) is said to be maximal monotone if it is monotone and its graph, \(\{(x, y) \in H \times H : y \in T(x)\}\), is not properly contained in the graph of any other monotone operator.

items.name: Cocoercivity with respect to the solution set
items.statement:
An operator \(B\) is said to be \(\beta\)-cocoercive with respect to the solution set \(S := (A + B)^{-1}(0)\) if
\[\langle B(x) - B(y), x - y \rangle \ge \beta|B(x) - B(y)|^2 \quad \forall x \in H,\; \forall y \in S,\]
where \(\beta > 0\) is a real number.

items.name: Resolvent of a maximal monotone operator
items.statement: For a maximal monotone operator \(T\), for each \(x \in H\) and \(\lambda > 0\) there is a unique \(z \in H\) such that \(x \in (I + \lambda T)z\). The single-valued operator \(J_{\lambda}^T := (I + \lambda T)^{-1}\) is called the resolvent of \(T\) of parameter \(\lambda\). It is a nonexpansive mapping which is everywhere defined and satisfies: \(z = J_{\lambda}^T z\) if and only if \(0 \in Tz\).

items.name: Opial's Lemma
items.statement:
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and \(\{x_k\}\) a sequence such that there exists a nonempty set \(S \subset H\) verifying:

- For every \(x^* \in S\), \(\lim_{k \to +\infty} |x_k - x^*|\) exists.
- If \(x_{k_j}\) weakly converges to \(x \in H\) for a subsequence \(k_j \to +\infty\), then \(x \in S\).

Then, there exists \(\tilde{x} \in S\) such that \(\{x_k\}\) weakly converges to \(\tilde{x}\) in \(H\).
items.proof: Cited from: Z. Opial, Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 73 (1967) 591–597.

items.name: Demclosedness of the graph of the ε-enlargement (Proposition 3.4)
items.statement:
Let \(T\) be a maximal monotone operator on a Banach space \(X\). The graph of the ε-enlargement \(T_{(\cdot)}(\cdot) : \mathbb{R}_+ \times X \to 2^{X^*}\) is demiclosed, i.e., the following conditions hold:

(a) If \(\{x_k\} \subset X\) converges strongly to \(x_0\), \(\{u_k \in T_{\varepsilon_k}(x_k)\}\) converges weak* to \(u_0\) in \(X^*\), and \(\{\varepsilon_k\} \subset \mathbb{R}_+\) converges to \(\varepsilon\), then \(u_0 \in T_{\varepsilon}(x_0)\).

(b) If \(\{x_k\} \subset X\) converges weakly to \(x_0\), \(\{u_k \in T_{\varepsilon_k}(x_k)\}\) converges strongly to \(u_0\) in \(X^*\), and \(\{\varepsilon_k\} \subset \mathbb{R}_+\) converges to \(\varepsilon\), then \(u_0 \in T_{\varepsilon}(x_0)\).
items.proof:
To prove (a), observe that since \(\{x_k\}\) converges strongly and \(\{u_k\}\) converges weak*, they are bounded sequences. Let \(M < +\infty\) be a bound for \(\|x_k\|\) and \(\|u_k\|\). Take any \((y, v) \in G(T)\). From Definition 2.1, it follows that

\[-\varepsilon_k \le \langle x_k - y, u_k - v \rangle = \langle x_k - y, u_0 - v \rangle + \langle x_k - y, u_k - u_0 \rangle\]

\[= \langle x_k - y, u_0 - v \rangle + \langle x_k - x_0, u_k - u_0 \rangle + \langle x_0 - y, u_k - u_0 \rangle\]

\[\le \langle x_k - y, u_0 - v \rangle + \|x_k - x_0\|(M + \|u_0\|) + \langle x_0 - y, u_k - u_0 \rangle.\]

Taking the limit \(k \to +\infty\), we obtain

\[-\varepsilon \le \langle x_0 - y, u_0 - v \rangle.\]

Since \((y, v)\) is an arbitrary element in the graph of \(T\), the conclusion \(u_0 \in T_{\varepsilon}(x_0)\) follows.

For proving item (b), recall that weak convergent sequences are also bounded and use a similar reasoning. \(\square\)

In the context of the Moudafi–Oliny paper (Hilbert space setting, where weak and weak* convergence coincide), part (b) with \(\varepsilon_k \to 0\) is used to pass from \(0 \in (A + B)_{\varepsilon_{k_j+1}}(x_{k_j+1})\) with \(x_{k_j+1} \rightharpoonup \bar{x}\) to the conclusion \(0 \in (A + B)(\bar{x})\), i.e., \(\bar{x} \in S\).

items.name: Convergence of the splitting inertial proximal method
items.statement:
Let \(\{x_k\} \subset H\) be a sequence generated by
\[\lambda_k A_{\varepsilon_k}(x_{k+1}) + x_{k+1} - y_k + \lambda_k B(x_k) \ni 0, \tag{1.6}\]
where \(y_k := x_k + \theta_k(x_k - x_{k-1})\), \(A, B\) are two maximal monotone operators with \(B\) \(\beta\)-cocoercive, and suppose that the parameters \(\theta_k, \lambda_k\) and \(\varepsilon_k\) satisfy:

1. \(\exists \delta, \exists \underline{\lambda} > 0\) such that \(\forall k \in \mathbb{N}^*\), \(\underline{\lambda} \le \lambda_k \le 2\beta - \delta\).
2. \(\exists \theta \in [0,1[\) such that \(\forall k \in \mathbb{N}^*\), \(0 \le \theta_k \le \theta\).
3. \(\sum_{k=1}^{+\infty} \varepsilon_k < +\infty\).

If the following condition holds
\[\sum_{k=1}^{+\infty} \theta_k|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 < +\infty, \tag{2.10}\]
then, there exists \(x^* \in S\) such that \(\{x_k\}\) weakly converges to \(x^*\) as \(k \to +\infty\).
items.proof:
Fix \(x \in S = T^{-1}(0)\) and set \(\phi_k = \frac{1}{2}|x - x_k|^2\). We have

\[\phi_k - \phi_{k+1} = \frac{1}{2}|x_{k+1} - x_k|^2 + \langle x_{k+1} - y_k, x - x_{k+1} \rangle + \theta_k\langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x - x_{k+1} \rangle, \tag{2.11}\]

where \(y_k := x_k + \theta_k(x_k - x_{k-1})\). Since \(-x_{k+1} + y_k - \lambda_k B(x_k) \in \lambda_k A_{\varepsilon_k}(x_{k+1})\) and \(-\lambda_k B(x) \in \lambda_k A(x)\), from definition (1.5) it follows that

\[\langle x_{k+1} - y_k + \lambda_k(B(x_k) - B(x)), x - x_{k+1} \rangle \ge -\lambda_k \varepsilon_k. \tag{2.12}\]

Combining (2.11) and (2.12), we obtain

\[\phi_k - \phi_{k+1} \ge \frac{1}{2}|x_{k+1} - x_k|^2 + \lambda_k\langle B(x_k) - B(x), x_{k+1} - x\rangle - \theta_k\langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_{k+1} - x\rangle - \lambda_k\varepsilon_k.\]

By invoking the equality

\[\langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_{k+1} - x\rangle = \langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_k - x\rangle + \langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_{k+1} - x_k\rangle\]

\[= \phi_k - \phi_{k-1} + \frac{1}{2}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 + \langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_{k+1} - x_k\rangle,\]

it follows that

\[\phi_{k+1} - \phi_k - \theta_k(\phi_k - \phi_{k-1}) \le -\frac{1}{2}|x_{k+1} - x_k|^2 + \theta_k\langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_{k+1} - x_k\rangle\]

\[+ \frac{\theta_k}{2}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 - \lambda_k\langle B(x_k) - B(x), x_{k+1} - x\rangle + \lambda_k\varepsilon_k.\]

On the other hand, since \(B\) is cocoercive, we get

\[\lambda_k\langle B(x_k) - B(x), x_{k+1} - x\rangle\]

\[= \lambda_k\big(\langle B(x_k) - B(x), x_k - x\rangle + \langle B(x_k) - B(x), x_{k+1} - x_k\rangle\big)\]

\[\ge \lambda_k\big(\beta|B(x_k) - B(x)|^2 + \langle B(x_k) - B(x), x_{k+1} - x_k\rangle\big)\]

\[\ge -\frac{\lambda_k}{4\beta}|x_{k+1} - x_k|^2.\]

From which we infer, by setting \(\eta_k := 1 - \lambda_k/(2\beta)\), the estimate (2.13) below

\[\phi_{k+1} - \phi_k - \theta_k(\phi_k - \phi_{k-1})\]

\[\le -\frac{1}{2}\eta_k|x_{k+1} - x_k|^2 + \theta_k\langle x_k - x_{k-1}, x_{k+1} - x_k\rangle + \frac{\theta_k}{2}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 + \lambda_k\varepsilon_k\]

\[\le -\frac{1}{2}\eta_k\left|x_{k+1} - \frac{\theta_k}{\eta_k} y_k\right|^2 + \frac{\theta_k^2}{2\eta_k}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 + \frac{\theta_k}{2}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 + \lambda_k\varepsilon_k\]

\[\le -\frac{1}{2}\eta_k\left|x_{k+1} - x_k - \frac{\theta_k}{\eta_k}(x_k - x_{k-1})\right|^2 + \frac{\theta_k}{\eta_k}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 + \lambda_k\varepsilon_k. \tag{2.13}\]

By taking into account the fact that from the hypotheses \(\eta_k\) is bounded and by setting \(\Delta_k := \phi_k - \phi_{k-1}\) and \(\sigma_k := \frac{2\beta\theta_k}{\delta}|x_k - x_{k-1}|^2 + \lambda_k\varepsilon_k\), we obtain

\[\Delta_{k+1} \le \theta_k\Delta_k + \sigma_k \le \theta_k[\Delta_k]_+ + \sigma_k,\]

where \([t]_+ := \max(t, 0)\), and consequently

\[[\Delta_{k+1}]_+ \le \theta[\Delta_k]_+ + \sigma_k\]

with \(\theta \in [0,1[\) given by hypothesis 2.

The latter inequality yields

\[[\Delta_{k+1}]_+ \le \theta^k[\Delta_1]_+ + \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \theta^i \sigma_{k-i}\]

and therefore

\[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} [\Delta_{k+1}]_+ \le \frac{1}{1-\theta}\left([\Delta_1]_+ + \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \sigma_k\right),\]

which is finite thanks to hypothesis 3 and (2.10). Consider the sequence defined by \(t_k := \phi_k - \sum_{i=1}^{k} [\Delta_i]_+\). Since \(\phi_k \ge 0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^{k} [\Delta_i]_+ < +\infty\), it follows that \(t_k\) is bounded from below. But

\[t_{k+1} = \phi_{k+1} - [\Delta_{k+1}]_+ - \sum_{i=1}^{k} [\Delta_i]_+ \le \phi_{k+1} - \phi_{k+1} + \phi_k - \sum_{i=1}^{k} [\Delta_i]_+ = t_k,\]

so that \(\{t_k\}\) is nonincreasing. We thus deduce that \(\{t_k\}\) is convergent and so is \(\{\phi_k\}\). This shows that the first condition of Opial's lemma is satisfied.

On the other hand, from (2.13) we can write

\[\frac{1}{2}\eta_k\left|x_{k+1} - x_k - \frac{\theta_k}{\eta_k}(x_k - x_{k-1})\right|^2 \le -\Delta_{k+1} + \theta\Delta_k + \sigma_k.\]

By passing to the limit in the above estimate and by taking into account the conditions on the parameters and the fact that by hypothesis \(|x_k - x_{k-1}| \to 0\), we obtain

\[\lim_{k \to +\infty} |x_{k+1} - x_k - \theta_k(x_k - x_{k-1})| = 0.\]

Now let \(\bar{x}\) be a weak cluster point of \(\{x_k\}\). There exists a subsequence \(\{x_{k_j}\}\) which converges weakly to \(\bar{x}\) and satisfies, thanks to (1.6),

\[-\frac{1}{\lambda_{k_j}}(x_{k_j+1} - y_{k_j}) + (B(x_{k_j+1}) - B(x_{k_j})) \in A_{\varepsilon_{k_j+1}}(x_{k_j+1}) + B(x_{k_j+1}) \subset (A + B)_{\varepsilon_{k_j+1}}(x_{k_j+1}).\]

Passing to the limit, as \(k_j \to +\infty\), using the fact that \(B\) is Lipschitz continuous and thanks to the properties of the enlargements \cite[Proposition 3.4]{SvaiterBurachik1999}, we obtain that \(0 \in (A + B)(\bar{x})\), that is \(\bar{x} \in S\).

Thus, the second condition of Opial's lemma is also satisfied, which completes the proof. \(\square\)
